data.description:
## Why

The outbound comment sync re-posted duplicate comments to Jira on every hourly pass
(bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` / `aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`: the PRIMARY comment-id dedup map
`comment_ids` was inert/empty, leaving only the lossy body-membership fallback). The
reconcile-bridge workflow is now **paused** (`disabled_manually`), so the duplicate set is
FIXED and no longer growing. ~30 Jira issues carry duplicates; **REB-1861** is pinned at
Jira's 5000-comment HARD cap (40 local comments, ~39 re-posted per pass), so new comments on
it silently fail with `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. **REB-1580** is next worst
(~21/pass). This ticket purges the accumulated duplicates.

This is the SAME failure class, via a different route, as bug `florid-vigorous-urial`
(`1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356`); its cleanup task `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` (extrovert-dippy-bongo) is the
established precedent and its mechanism is reused verbatim here rather than reinvented.

## Mechanism (reused from bd80 — see that ticket for the full rationale)

- **Bot-authored identification (safety-critical filter).** A Jira comment is a deletion
  candidate IFF the RENDERED text of its ADF body contains
  `RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"`
  (`outbound_comments.py`, appended by `_decorate_outbound_comment`). Rendering uses the same
  path `_normalize_comment_body` uses (`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` → `adf.adf_to_text`).
  A comment whose rendered text lacks the marker is treated as human/foreign and is NEVER a
  deletion candidate.
- **Secondary cross-check.** All marked candidates must resolve to a single bot
  `author.accountId`; a divergent accountId on a marked comment aborts that issue for manual
  review.
- **Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization.** Group candidates by
  `outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body)` — imported and reused verbatim, not
  re-implemented — so the cleanup's notion of "distinct body" is identical to the reconciler's.
- **Keep-one rule.** Per distinct normalized body among MARKED comments: keep the OLDEST copy
  (min `created`) and delete the rest. A distinct body with only ONE copy is NEVER deleted.
  Unmarked comments are never touched.
- **Pagination.** Full comment set via the paginated fetch; completeness is reconciled against
  the `total` from `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?maxResults=0`. `len(fetched) != total`
  REFUSES to proceed for that issue.
- **Deletion.** `DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id}` via the client's `delete_comment`,
  throttled, 404 treated as idempotent success, appended to a JSONL deletion log as it happens
  (resumable).

## Safety plan (T4 — irreversible)

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup** of the FULL comment payload (id, rendered body, ADF body,
      author.accountId, created) per issue, written and completeness-checked BEFORE any DELETE.
- [ ] **Dry-run default.** The script only deletes under an explicit `--execute`; the dry-run
      prints per issue: total, marked count, distinct-body count, kept id per body, delete count.
- [ ] **Canary first.** Execute on ONE light issue, verify fully, then proceed.
      **REB-1861 is done LAST** (largest, riskiest).
- [ ] **Per-issue post-verification**: after deletion, re-fetch and assert the surviving set
      still contains exactly one copy of every distinct normalized body present before.
- [ ] **Workflow stays paused** for the whole operation; it is NOT re-enabled by this ticket.
- [ ] Ambiguous cases are SKIPPED and reported, never guessed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Backup artifact exists per issue and passes `len(fetched) == reported total` before any
      deletion.
- [ ] Dry-run output produced and inspected before `--execute`.
- [ ] Every affected issue is below the 5000 cap after the run; REB-1861 specifically drops from
      5000 to its distinct-body count.
- [ ] For every issue touched, a post-deletion re-fetch confirms every distinct normalized body
      present before the run still has exactly one surviving copy (zero content loss).
- [ ] No unmarked/human comment is deleted anywhere.
- [ ] A deletion log (ticket, comment id, body hash, outcome) exists for the executed run.
data.title: Jira data cleanup: purge duplicate comments from the ~30 issues inflated by the inert comment-id dedup (bd80 precedent)
